messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - GPU autoscaler failing in prod (inference-ns). Observed: queue growth + throttling. Possible root: custom metric lag from prometheus-adapter. Paging oncall.

sarah (oncall): saw the alert, acking. pulling up dashboards now.

raj (eng-sre): I can join, prepping kubectl creds. which cluster? prod-us-east1?

sarah (oncall): yes prod-us-east1. symptom: sustained GPU queue_length > 400 for 10m, HPA not scaling beyond 8 replicas (max 8 configured). clients getting 429s and 30s+ waits.

emily (runtime): looking at serving runtime traces — requests queued at the gate layer, tokens being chunked. RTs spiking.

julia (eng-ml): seeing model fallback triggered for some traffic. quality regressions flagged for smaller variants.

raj (eng-sre): running quick checks. `kubectl -n inference get hpa inference-gpu -o yaml`

raj (eng-sre): HPA shows lastScaleTime 2026-12-02T12:34:00Z, currentReplicas: 8, desiredReplicas: 8, maxReplicas: 8. metrics: custom/gpu.queue_length: "No data" reported by adapter.

sarah (oncall): that matches prometheus-adapter being flaky. can we query Prom?

emily (runtime): `curl -s 'https://prom.prod/api/v1/query?query=gpu_queue_length%7Benv=%22prod%22%7D' | jq '.data'` returning empty for most pods, `prom-adapter` logs show 504s to Prom.

raj (eng-sre): `kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter --tail=200` shows: "error: upstream request timed out" and repeated 502/504. scrape latency for prometheus is 90-120s on some targets.

sarah (oncall): customer-impact: CS reported multiple customers with elevated latency and client-side rate-limited errors. Mike from product on call?

mike (product): here — priority is to reduce customer-facing 429s asap. what quick mitigations possible?

julia (eng-ml): could temporarily relax HPA maxReplicas to allow manual scaling if metrics remain absent. also consider a manual scale to cover backlog.

raj (eng-sre): agreed. plan: 1) temporarily bump HPA maxReplicas to 24, 2) manually scale inference-deployment to 20 replicas, 3) restart prometheus-adapter pods, 4) if adapter still fails, fallback: switch HPA to use internal queue-length from runtime exporter (if available) or pause HPA and monitor.

sarah (oncall): doing step 1 and 2 now. `kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-gpu -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":24}}'` -> applied.

sarah (oncall): `kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-gpu --replicas=20` -> scaling started. node autoscaler kicking in for GPU nodepool. estimated time ~4-6m.

emily (runtime): enabling temporary rate-limit on public route to 20r/s to slow intake. pushing rule to API gateway now.

customer-support: posting status to affected customers: "We're experiencing autoscaling delays leading to elevated latency and throttling; mitigation in progress, ETA 10–15m."

raj (eng-sre): restarting prometheus-adapter: `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deploy/prometheus-adapter` -> restarted 3 pods.

raj (eng-sre): checking adapter logs... pod-1 shows `200` on some queries now, pod-2 still hit 504s. seeing connection saturation to Prom; digging traffic.

emily (runtime): while nodes spin up, queued requests dropping slowly as replicas come ready. latency improving for some customers.

sarah (oncall): HPA now sees some metrics: `kubectl -n inference get hpa` -> desiredReplicas=18, currentReplicas=12. nice.

julia (eng-ml): note: model batching and KV cache warms slowly — cold-starts may still produce degraded latency for some requests.

mike (product): can we route high-priority customers to dedicated pool or smaller models to reduce SLA impact?

emily (runtime): we can route to dedicated capacity for top-tier customers, I'll open a rule and shift 10% of traffic.

raj (eng-sre): prometheus shows scrape backlog cleared after adapter restart and reducing scrape concurrency. Prometheus write load temporarily high due to node metrics burst. We increased adapter timeouts to 30s.

sarah (oncall): monitoring: queue_length trending down to 50s, 429 count decreasing.

customer-support: updated customers: "Mitigation: additional replicas added, autoscaler max increased, adapter restarted. We expect stabilization in 5–10m. Apologies for the disruption." :thumbsup:

raj (eng-sre): follow-ups to create: 1) increase HPA maxReplicas headroom for peak times, 2) add circuit-breaker for prom-adapter upstream errors, 3) add fallback metric (runtime exporter) for HPA, 4) run load test to reproduce adapter saturation, 5) automate manual-scale runbook. assigning now.

mike (product): also capture customer list for postmortem communication.

julia (eng-ml): creating eval run to verify model fallback quality impact during similar mitigations.

sarah (oncall): marking incident as "mitigated" for now. will keep channel open for 1h for stability checks. filing incident ticket and linking this thread.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1429, severity P1 -> assigned to oncall.

sarah (oncall): handing off to raj for postmortem work. I'm going offline for rotation.

raj (eng-sre): taking over. I'll collect logs, timeline, and draft RCA. thanks all.

customer-support: closing outbound loop after postmortem ready.

emily (runtime): note for RCA: consider adding rate-limits that adapt based on adapter health and queue depth.

sarah (oncall): good call. tagging as action item.

raj (eng-sre): last check: 429/s down 95%, queue_length <30, nodes stable. closing active mitigations. will post RCA within 48h.

mike (product): thanks team.
